quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #11
										  					
  

25 Questions • Passing Score 22

questions.question: What does a red curb mean?

options.text: Loading zone.
You can pick up or drop off passengers here.
No parking, standing, or stopping.

questions.correctAnswerText: No parking, standing, or stopping.
questions.explanation: You cannot stop, stand, or park at a red curb.

questions.question: Which statement about blind spots is true?

options.text: One outside mirror eliminates blind spots.
Large trucks have bigger blind spots than most cars.
You can see blind spots in your rearview mirror.

questions.correctAnswerText: Large trucks have bigger blind spots than most cars.
questions.explanation: Even with mirrors, all vehicles have blind spots you cannot see. Large trucks have much larger blind spots than most cars.

questions.question: An emergency vehicle with flashing lights is behind you. What should you do?

options.text: Drive to the right and slow down.
Drive to the right and stop.
Stay in your lane, slow down, and let it pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drive to the right and stop.
questions.explanation: You must give the right-of-way to emergency vehicles using sirens and lights. Drive to the right edge of the road and stop. If you are in an intersection, drive through it first, then stop.

questions.question: How can you avoid skidding on slippery surfaces?

options.text: Shift to a lower gear after starting down a steep hill.
Speed up to enter curves and slow down to exit them.
Slow down before entering curves and intersections.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down before entering curves and intersections.
questions.explanation: Slow down before you enter a curve because you cannot see what is ahead. Braking while turning can cause you to skid.

questions.question: What does a broken yellow line next to a solid yellow line mean?

options.text: You can pass from the lane next to the solid line.
No one can pass from either direction.
You can pass from the lane next to the broken line.

questions.correctAnswerText: You can pass from the lane next to the broken line.
questions.explanation: A broken yellow line next to a solid yellow line means drivers in the lane with the broken line can pass. Drivers in the lane with the solid line cannot pass.

questions.question: What does a blood alcohol level of 0.02 percent do?

options.text: It has no effect on your driving.
It does not put other drivers at risk.
It doubles your chance of having an accident.

questions.correctAnswerText: It doubles your chance of having an accident.
questions.explanation: Each 0.02 percent increase in blood alcohol nearly doubles your risk of a fatal crash.

questions.question: What should you do when driving on snow or ice?

options.text: It is safe to use cruise control.
Make speed and direction changes slowly and gradually.
Drive as you would in normal conditions.

questions.correctAnswerText: Make speed and direction changes slowly and gradually.
questions.explanation: On snow or ice, make speed and direction changes gradually. Never use cruise control on snow or ice because your tires may slip and you will lose control.

questions.question: What does this sign warn you about?

options.text: Upcoming intersections.
Road construction.
Road curves ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Road curves ahead.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black markings. They alert you to hazards ahead. This sign warns you of an upcoming curve to the right.

questions.question: As you drive faster, what is important to do?

options.text: Turn on your headlights.
Look far ahead of your vehicle.
Change lanes frequently.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look far ahead of your vehicle.
questions.explanation: Higher speeds require longer stopping distances. When driving fast, look far ahead so you have time to safely react to hazards.

questions.question: What should a driver do about right-of-way?

options.text: Assume all drivers obey right-of-way rules.
Assume most drivers obey right-of-way rules.
Always be ready to yield the right-of-way.

questions.correctAnswerText: Always be ready to yield the right-of-way.
questions.explanation: Right-of-way rules are guidelines, but no one should assume they have the right-of-way. Always be ready to yield if it prevents a collision.

questions.question: If you must park your vehicle in an unusual spot, what should you do?

options.text: Park with your reverse lights on.
Make sure drivers can see your vehicle from all directions.
Park five feet from the curb.

questions.correctAnswerText: Make sure drivers can see your vehicle from all directions.
questions.explanation: You must make sure your parked vehicle is not a hazard. Park where drivers approaching from any direction can see your car.

questions.question: Hydroplaning happens when tires slide on water instead of gripping the road. How can you prevent it in wet weather?

options.text: Use cruise control to keep a steady speed.
Slow down.
Move to the shoulder as soon as it rains.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down.
questions.explanation: Hydroplaning happens when you drive too fast on a wet road. Slow down on wet pavement to prevent hydroplaning.

questions.question: When can you make a left turn at a red light after stopping?

options.text: When turning from a two-way street onto a two-way street.
When turning from a one-way street onto another one-way street.
When you yield to all other traffic at the intersection.

questions.correctAnswerText: When turning from a one-way street onto another one-way street.
questions.explanation: After stopping, you may turn left at a red light only if you are on a one-way street and turning onto another one-way street. Check for any posted signs that ban this turn.

questions.question: Can you drive off the road to pass another vehicle?

options.text: Yes, if the vehicle ahead is turning left.
Yes, if there are two or more lanes going your direction.
No, never.

questions.correctAnswerText: No, never.
questions.explanation: You may never drive off the road or onto the shoulder to pass another vehicle.

questions.question: Which statement about large trucks is true?

options.text: They need more distance to stop than passenger vehicles.
They all have air brakes that let them stop quickly.
They are easier to maneuver than passenger vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: They need more distance to stop than passenger vehicles.
questions.explanation: Large trucks take much longer to stop. A passenger vehicle at 55 mph stops in about 400 feet. A large truck at the same speed needs almost 800 feet to stop.

questions.question: What should you do when driving through work zones?

options.text: Speed up to get through quickly.
Slow down and be ready to stop quickly.
Keep your normal speed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and be ready to stop quickly.
questions.explanation: When entering a work zone, slow down and be prepared to stop. Follow posted speed limits and stay alert. Workers may be present.

questions.question: What does a yellow left turn arrow mean?

options.text: Get ready to yield to oncoming traffic.
The protected left turn is ending.
Both of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: Both of the above.
questions.explanation: A yellow left arrow means the protected turn is ending. You must prepare to yield to oncoming traffic.

questions.question: When must you use your low beams?

options.text: On a lighted street.
On a freeway.
In fog.

questions.correctAnswerText: In fog.
questions.explanation: Use low beams in fog, snow, rain, or mist. High beams reflect off water and create glare, making it harder to see. Use low beams with fog lights if your vehicle has them.

questions.question: When should you not use your horn?

options.text: When you cannot see far ahead.
If you might hit another vehicle.
Near blind pedestrians.

questions.correctAnswerText: Near blind pedestrians.
questions.explanation: Do not use your horn near blind pedestrians. It can be dangerous. Yield to the pedestrian and go when it is safe.

questions.question: If oncoming headlights are blinding you at night, what should you do?

options.text: Look toward the right edge of the road.
Switch to high beams.
Turn your lights on and off.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look toward the right edge of the road.
questions.explanation: If oncoming headlights blind you, look at the right edge of the road instead of ahead. This keeps your vehicle on the road until you pass the other car.

questions.question: What are all drivers under 21 not allowed to do?

options.text: Drive while smoking.
Drive before midnight.
Drive after drinking any alcohol.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drive after drinking any alcohol.
questions.explanation: Drivers under 21 cannot drink alcohol. If you are stopped and have been drinking, your license will be suspended or revoked. You may also be charged for breaking the alcohol rule on your license.

questions.question: You are on the freeway behind a large truck. How should you drive?

options.text: Close behind the truck in bad weather because the driver can see farther ahead.
Farther behind the truck than you would behind a regular car.
No more than one car length behind the truck so the driver can see you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Farther behind the truck than you would behind a regular car.
questions.explanation: If you drive too close behind a truck, the truck driver cannot see you in their mirrors. Tailgating any vehicle is dangerous because you lose your safety space if the vehicle stops suddenly.

questions.question: What does a five-sided sign mean?

options.text: Stop sign.
Regulatory sign.
School zone or school crossing sign.

questions.correctAnswerText: School zone or school crossing sign.
questions.explanation: A five-sided sign warns drivers about school zones. Some show where children or pedestrians may cross the road near schools.

questions.question: The center line has one solid yellow line and one broken yellow line. The broken line is next to your lane. What does this mean?

options.text: You cannot pass in this area.
You can pass other vehicles on the left if no oncoming traffic is coming.
You can only make right turns in this area.

questions.correctAnswerText: You can pass other vehicles on the left if no oncoming traffic is coming.
questions.explanation: When you see a solid yellow line and a broken yellow line, you can pass from the side with the broken line.

questions.question: You are driving behind a motorcycle and want to pass. What must you do?

options.text: Stay in the right lane because the motorcycle is small and does not use the full lane.
Blow your horn to make the motorcycle move to the shoulder so you can pass.
Move your vehicle completely into the left lane before and during the pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move your vehicle completely into the left lane before and during the pass.
questions.explanation: When passing a motorcycle, give the full lane to the motorcycle. Do not share the lane. Returning to the right lane too soon can force the rider to swerve and crash.
